sections.h2: Where is Leesburg, VA, and what is its role in Loudoun County?
sections.html:
Leesburg is a town and the county seat of Loudoun County, about 33 miles west-northwest of Washington, D.C. at the base of Catoctin Mountain, according to Wikipedia. It covers 12.47 square miles at an elevation near 341 feet and is Virginia's largest incorporated town within a county.

Leesburg has been Loudoun's seat since the county formed in 1757. The current courthouse dates from 1894 and is one of the few Virginia courthouses that was not burned in the Civil War. Leesburg's courthouse is a landmark, and the county government is the town's largest employer.

sections.h2: What is Leesburg's history, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The Virginia General Assembly founded Leesburg on October 12, 1758, on 60 acres laid out by Nicholas Minor in six crossing streets. During the War of 1812 the town sheltered federal documents, including the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution, when Washington was threatened.

Early in the Civil War the Battle of Ball's Bluff was fought about 2 miles northeast of the town center, and Leesburg changed hands several times. The Leesburg historic district was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1970.

If your house is in or near the old downtown, it may carry added rules for exterior changes.

sections.h2: How did Leesburg change from a rural town to a commuter hub?
sections.html:
Leesburg went from 1,703 residents in 1950 to 16,202 in 1990, 28,311 in 2000 and 42,616 in 2010. The 2020 census counted 48,250. Wikipedia describes the change as a move from a small rural Piedmont town to a suburban community for commuters to the capital.

Growth concentrates along the Dulles Greenway and State Route 7. The housing stock therefore ranges from nineteenth century downtown houses to subdivisions built in the last several decades, and those two kinds of houses sell on very different terms.

Government and aviation lead the list. The town's FY 2022 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, as summarized by Wikipedia, ranked the top employers:

  • Loudoun County Government: 2,500 to 5,000 employees
  • Loudoun County Public Schools: 1,000 to 1,500
  • Federal Aviation Administration: 500 to 1,000
  • Town of Leesburg, Wegmans, the Commonwealth of Virginia, Target, Stryker and Costco: 250 to 500 each
  • Loudoun Medical Group: 100 to 250

The FAA's Washington Air Route Traffic Control Center is in Leesburg. Leesburg Executive Airport at Godfrey Field is a reliever airport for Dulles, and a 2011 state study put its economic impact at nearly $78 million a year.

sections.h2: Who lives in Leesburg, and what green space is nearby?
sections.html:
The median age in the 2020 census was 35.6. About 26.8 percent of residents were under 18 and 9.4 percent were 65 or older. Of 16,184 households, 42.4 percent had children, and 57.7 percent were married-couple households. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.6 percent and the rental vacancy rate was 4.8 percent.

Parks shape how neighborhoods feel. Ida Lee Park grew from a 141-acre farm donated to the town in 1986. Morven Park is a 1,000-acre historic estate and horse park. Red Rock Wilderness Overlook Regional Park has 67 acres and more than 2 miles of trails above the Potomac, and the Rust Sanctuary sits at the foot of Catoctin Mountain.

Annual events include the Flower and Garden Festival in April, a Fourth of July parade, a classic car show on the first Saturday in June, an airshow on the last Saturday in September and a long-running Halloween parade.

sections.h2: Which roads and schools serve Leesburg?
sections.html:
U.S. Route 15, State Route 7 and State Route 267 serve the town. Route 15 and Route 7 meet on the Leesburg Bypass, and Route 267, the Dulles Greenway, ends at the bypass. Route 7 runs about 37 miles west to Winchester and 35 miles southeast to Alexandria. Loudoun County Transit runs commuter routes to Washington and a connector to Purcellville.

The W&OD Railroad Regional Park, a 45-mile rail trail, runs through town.

Public schools are run by Loudoun County Public Schools. Wikipedia lists four high schools that serve Leesburg: Loudoun County, Heritage, Tuscarora and Riverside. Private options include Providence Academy, Evergreen Christian School and Loudoun Country Day School. Attendance boundaries change, so confirm them for a given address.

sections.h2: How are Leesburg real estate taxes billed?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2019, Loudoun County has billed and collected real estate tax for the Town of Leesburg. Owners get one bill that shows the county and town taxes and make one payment to the County of Loudoun.

The town's 2026 rate is $0.1774 per $100 of assessed value. The Loudoun County Commissioner of the Revenue assesses property each January at fair market value, and taxes are calculated on 100 percent of assessed value. Tax relief eligibility is decided by the county, so applications go there.

The town still collects delinquent taxes for 2018 and earlier. For those years it charges a 10 percent penalty (a $2 minimum, capped at the amount of the tax) and 10 percent annual interest. Later years go to the county's Treasurer. The Town of Leesburg tax page has the details.

Because the county bills, you will find due dates on Loudoun County's tax pages rather than the town's.

sections.h2: What do Leesburg sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Sellers here tend to meet a few recurring situations.

  • A downtown or older house that needs updating before it will appraise well.
  • An inherited home with several heirs spread across the region.
  • A rental that needs to be sold with or without tenants.
  • A relocation with a fixed date, including federal and county employees.

A cash sale is one option beside a listing. It avoids the buyer's financing and appraisal steps, but you should still compare the net amount, including repairs and carrying costs you would pay on a listing.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Leesburg?
sections.html:
The process starts with a conversation about the house and a written offer. If you accept, a title or settlement company searches the records, pays off any lien and handles the recording. You pick the closing date within what the title work allows.

Have the deed, your mortgage payoff information and any estate paperwork ready. A consolidated county and town tax bill makes the tax part of closing simpler, because there is only one account to check.

Ask any buyer for the offer in writing, confirm who pays for title and settlement charges, and read the closing statement before you sign. If a family member must approve the sale, bring them into the conversation before an offer arrives, so the closing date is not held up by a signature.

faqs.q: Is Leesburg a city or a town?
faqs.a: Leesburg is an incorporated town and the county seat of Loudoun County. With 48,250 residents in 2020, it is Virginia's largest incorporated town within a county.

faqs.q: Who bills Leesburg real estate taxes?
faqs.a: Loudoun County bills and collects them for the town. Owners receive one bill listing both county and town taxes.

faqs.q: What is the Leesburg real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The town lists a 2026 rate of $0.1774 per $100 of assessed value. The county's own rate is separate, so check the county's tax pages.

faqs.q: When does Loudoun County assess Leesburg property?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue assesses real estate each January at fair market value. Taxes are figured on 100 percent of assessed value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Leesburg house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is cash sale means you do not repair anything first, and the offer reflects the condition of the house.
